item.text:
Research continuation completed across all eight chapters. No score was assigned.

The repository shell remains unavailable (`bwrap: loopback: Failed RTM_NEWADDR`), so I could not update `research-ledger-manifest.json`; the additions below are ready for manifest reconciliation.

### 1B

- `G-1B-08`: Türkiye acceded to the Joint Convention on spent-fuel and radioactive-waste safety; UN Treaty registration dated 16 March 2023, with accession effective 20 February 2023. This is a target-period nonproliferation/safety action attributable to the state, but not necessarily personally directed by Erdoğan. [UN Treaty Collection](https://treaties.un.org/Pages/showActionDetails.aspx?clang=_en&objid=080000028060e7c0)
- `G-1B-09`: Türkiye participated in the 29 June 2023 Non-Proliferation and Disarmament Initiative working paper on transparency, accountability, and NPT review. [UN Digital Library](https://digitallibrary.un.org/record/4015876)
- `G-1B-10`: The IAEA recorded first nuclear fuel arrival at Akkuyu in April 2023 and described the plant as Türkiye’s first nuclear power plant. This documents peaceful nuclear expansion and safety-governance relevance, not weapons acquisition. [IAEA](https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/news/iaea-chief-highlights-sustainable-energy-as-first-nuclear-fuel-arrives-in-turkiye)
- `G-1B-11`: Türkiye’s 2023 accession to the radioactive-waste Joint Convention provides contrary evidence to a purely “no nuclear governance” characterization. The evidence remains institutional rather than ruler-personal.

Shortfall: no 2023 Erdoğan speech or directive changing nuclear doctrine, nuclear-sharing command, or weapons posture was recovered.

### 2B

- `G-2B-12`: Türkiye’s Foreign Ministry stated in February 2023 that it supported negotiations to end the Ukraine war and the Istanbul Grain Deal. This is direct official evidence of mediation posture. [Turkish MFA](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/no_-56_-ukrayna-savasinin-birinci-yili-hk.en.mfa)
- `G-2B-13`: A June 2023 Türkiye–US strategic dialogue welcomed continued cooperation on the Grain Initiative and peaceful resolution of the Ukraine war. [Turkish MFA](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/no_-156_-turkiye--amerika-birlesik-devletleri-strategic-mechanism-dialogue.en.mfa)
- `G-2B-14`: NATO Secretary General confirmed that Erdoğan submitted Sweden’s accession protocol on 23 October 2023 and that Sweden had amended laws, expanded counterterrorism cooperation, and resumed arms exports. [NATO](https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/news_219526.htm)
- `G-2B-15`: The Northeast Syria NGO Forum documented 24 strikes, five civilian injuries, and damage near Washokani camp on 5–6 October 2023; water and electricity disruption affected displaced populations. [ReliefWeb](https://reliefweb.int/report/syrian-arab-republic/escalation-hostilities-targeting-critical-civilian-infrastructures-northeast-syria)
- `G-2B-16`: HRW documented that Turkish border forces killed two Syrians and tortured others in March 2023, while six soldiers entered pretrial detention. This supplies both abuse evidence and contrary accountability evidence. [HRW](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/04/27/turkish-border-guards-torture-kill-syrians)

### 3B

- `G-3B-11`: HRW documented 11 deaths and 20 injuries caused by Turkish border guards during early 2023, while six guards were investigated for the March 11 incident. [HRW](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/04/27/turkish-border-guards-torture-kill-syrians)
- `G-3B-12`: Istanbul police detained 113 Pride participants on 25 June 2023; the Istanbul governor publicly justified the ban by referring to events threatening “the institution of the family.” [HRW](https://www.hrw.org/news/2023/06/27/turkey-mass-detentions-pride-marches)
- `G-3B-13`: The Council of Europe Committee of Ministers again called for Osman Kavala’s and Selahattin Demirtaş’s immediate release in March 2023 and requested judicial-independence measures. [Council of Europe](https://www.coe.int/en/web/execution/-/t%C3%BCrkiye-the-committee-of-ministers-reiterates-calls-for-the-immediate-release-of-osman-kavala-and-selahattin-demirta%C5%9F)
- `G-3B-14`: The Turkish government’s documented investigation of six border guards and prosecution of three soldiers is contrary evidence that remedies were entirely absent; the record does not establish whether the remedies were effective or complete.

### 4B

- `G-4B-15`: ODIHR’s official preliminary report states that the election offered voters a genuine choice, while YSP faced pervasive pressure and systematic detentions. [ODIHR preliminary report, pp. 13–14](https://odihr.osce.org/sites/default/files/f/documents/6/2/543543.pdf)
- `G-4B-16`: ODIHR recorded 861 polling stations merged or relocated, potentially affecting 57,170 voters, and noted that some interlocutors considered the changes politically motivated. [ODIHR, p. 10](https://odihr.osce.org/sites/default/files/f/documents/6/2/543543.pdf)
- `G-4B-17`: ODIHR recorded that government officials breached restrictions on using official events and state resources for campaigning. [ODIHR, p. 13](https://odihr.osce.org/sites/default/files/f/documents/6/2/543543.pdf)
- `G-4B-18`: ODIHR also recorded that election-day polling was generally well organized and positively assessed in most observed stations, providing institutional counterevidence to claims of wholly nonfunctional administration. [ODIHR, pp. 21–22](https://odihr.osce.org/sites/default/files/f/documents/6/2/543543.pdf)
- `G-4B-19`: The ODIHR final-report page confirms the mission’s complete 2023 coverage, including the 28 May runoff and September final assessment. [OSCE/ODIHR](https://odihr.osce.org/odihr/elections/turkiye/553963)

### 5B

- `G-5B-10`: IMF staff reported in October 2023 that post-election rate increases, tax measures, and financial liberalization reduced risks, lifted investor confidence, compressed spreads, and improved CBRT reserves. [IMF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/10/06/pr23343-turkiye-imf-staff-concludes-staff-visit-to-turkiye)
- `G-5B-11`: The same IMF assessment projected 4% growth in 2023 but expected inflation near 69% at year-end and warned that reserves net of short-term liabilities remained negative. This provides independent contrary evidence to any simple stabilization claim. [IMF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/10/06/pr23343-turkiye-imf-staff-concludes-staff-visit-to-turkiye)
- `G-5B-12`: The European Commission’s 2023 Türkiye report identified weak procurement transparency and competition, and strengthened allegations of political influence over procurement. [European Commission report](https://ab.gov.tr/siteimages/birimler/kpb/trkiye_report_2023.pdf)
- `G-5B-13`: The World Bank estimated $34.2 billion in direct earthquake damage and stated that recovery costs could be roughly twice as high, documenting a major fiscal and household shock. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/02/27/earthquake-damage-in-turkiye-estimated-to-exceed-34-billion-world-bank-disaster-assessment-report)

Shortfall: no clean 2023 household-quintile, productivity, investment, or named personal corruption record was recovered.

### 6B

- `G-6B-11`: The World Bank approved $1 billion in June 2023 for restoring health services, municipal infrastructure, and resilient rural housing across 11 earthquake-affected provinces. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/06/27/world-bank-approves-1-billion-for-turkiye-to-help-restore-rural-homes-and-essential-public-services-to-people-in-earthqu)
- `G-6B-12`: The World Bank reported that newer schools built to updated seismic standards largely withstood the earthquakes, while around 5% of education buildings in affected areas collapsed or were moderately/severely damaged. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/feature/2023/06/07/how-safer-and-more-resilient-schools-withstood-the-earthquakes-in-türkiye)
- `G-6B-13`: UNHCR’s 2023 Türkiye results report records more than 58,000 Syrian refugee youth enrolled in higher education, approximately 14%, with 44% female participation. [UNHCR 2023 results report](https://reporting.unhcr.org/sites/default/files/2024-06/Europe%20-%20Tu%CC%88rkiye%20ARR%202023.pdf)
- `G-6B-14`: UNHCR documents national access for refugees to education, healthcare, labor-market participation, and social assistance, including conditional cash transfers for education. [UNHCR](https://www.unhcr.org/tr/en/ne-yapiyoruz/education)
- `G-6B-15`: Türkiye’s investment authority reported three million evacuations, 433,000 tents, 3.7 million daily meals, and emergency cash assistance after the earthquake. This is official administrative-capacity evidence, although it should be kept distinct from independent outcome verification. [Invest in Türkiye](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/news/news-from-turkey/pages/turkish-government-introduces-new-earthquake-recovery-measures.aspx)

Shortfall: fresh 2023 national health, education, maternal-mortality, immunization, and post-earthquake service-outcome series remain unavailable.

### 7B

- `G-7B-15`: The European Commission’s 2023 report identifies weak procurement transparency and competition, plus allegations of political influence over procurement. This is institutional integrity evidence, not personal enrichment evidence. [European Commission](https://ab.gov.tr/siteimages/birimler/kpb/trkiye_report_2023.pdf)
- `G-7B-16`: The Turkish Constitutional Court’s 2023 annual report records activity concerning transparency, accountability, and public procurement disputes, supplying evidence that formal review institutions continued operating. [Constitutional Court annual report](https://www.anayasa.gov.tr/media/9238/2023_annual_report.pdf)
- `G-7B-17`: Erdoğan publicly acknowledged shortcomings in earthquake response and asked forgiveness, while qualifying the admission by citing tremors and bad weather. [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-64789135)
- `G-7B-18`: The IMF independently described the post-election policy shift as reducing risks and improving investor confidence, providing contrary evidence to an account portraying all 2023 policy communication as deceptive or purely opportunistic. [IMF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/10/06/pr23343-turkiye-imf-staff-concludes-staff-visit-to-turkiye)

Shortfall: no primary 2023 asset declaration, beneficial-ownership, family-contract, or personal procurement record was recovered. Country corruption indicators remain contextual only.

### 8B

- `G-8B-15`: The official World Bank project approved in June 2023 translated earthquake recovery into defined components: health services, municipal infrastructure, and resilient rural housing. [World Bank project record](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099061423141522303)
- `G-8B-16`: The Turkish government reported concrete response outputs: evacuation, tents, meals, cash aid, and housing groundbreakings. These are official implementation claims and require independent verification. [Invest in Türkiye](https://www.invest.gov.tr/en/news/news-from-turkey/pages/turkish-government-introduces-new-earthquake-recovery-measures.aspx)
- `G-8B-17`: IMF staff independently confirmed that rate increases, tax measures, and financial liberalization reduced risks and lifted investor confidence by October 2023. [IMF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2023/10/06/pr23343-turkiye-imf-staff-concludes-staff-visit-to-turkiye)
- `G-8B-18`: NATO independently confirmed the October 2023 Sweden protocol submission and identified the reciprocal commitments behind the agreement. [NATO](https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/news_219526.htm)
- `G-8B-19`: Türkiye’s MFA documented continuing mediation efforts around the Grain Initiative and Ukraine negotiations, adding a peaceful-diplomacy implementation track. [Turkish MFA](https://www.mfa.gov.tr/no_-56_-ukrayna-savasinin-birinci-yili-hk.en.mfa)
- `G-8B-20`: The European Commission’s 2023 report provides contrary evidence on implementation quality by identifying weak procurement transparency, limited competition, and political-influence concerns. [European Commission](https://ab.gov.tr/siteimages/birimler/kpb/trkiye_report_2023.pdf)

### Rejected or limited candidates

- Direct IMF 2023 Article IV full report: now partially recovered through the official October 2023 staff-visit page; the previously inaccessible 2024 publication is not needed for the target-period claim.
- OSCE/ODIHR election evidence: no longer gateway-only; the official PDF and final-report page were recovered.
- UN/IAEA nuclear material: retained as institutional evidence, but not converted into personal Erdoğan attribution.
- Government earthquake statistics: retained as official self-report and explicitly separated from independent World Bank/UN evidence.
- 2024–2026 retrospective claims: excluded from target-period event claims except where they document the status of a 2023 institution or action.

The evidence remains uneven: 1B, 5B, 6B, and 7B still have attribution or outcome gaps, while 2B, 3B, 4B, and 8B gained several primary or independent locators.
